response.reason: This lens contrasts the NL-derived contract structure with exact FCSTM/source identities: the root initial edge, the InMotion-owned initial edge into Accelerating, the InMotion group topology (which was rewired through a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state and a route-token guard mechanism), containment/cardinality of InMotion's three substates, and the event-consumer coverage for Reached_Cruising_Cruise, Approached_Decelerate, and Obstacle_Detected. NL1-INIT-1 (root->DoorsClosing) is satisfied by tr line 37/2. NL5-INIT-1 (InMotion-owned initial entering Accelerating) is violated: InMotion's own initial pseudostate edge (transition:line:18) targets the synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state, not Accelerating, so the owner-local edge does not reach the required target -- this is an exact S2 violation for the InMotion-owned initial-entry contract, independent of the satisfied root->DoorsClosing entry. All endpoint contracts NL5/NL6/NL7-ENDPOINT-1 (Accelerating->Cruising, Accelerating->Approaching, Cruising->Approaching) are present as exact transitions (line19/20/21) even though those states are unreachable from initial; per frontier discipline reachability defects are captured separately (already an existing initial_entry contract) and do not turn the satisfied endpoints into wrong-target issues, so they are omitted. NL2-ENDPOINT-1/2 (InMotion->Stopping, InMotion->EmergencyStopping) exist at model level (line 35/36) using guarded R45RouteToken transitions rather than the named NL triggers; the actual carrying transitions have guard-based routing instead of the direct named signal triggers, but since exact source/target states match I omit S2 wrong-target candidates for these, but I flag the trigger/guard mismatch under NL2-DISJOINT-1 and a derived group-relation contract. Containment contracts NL4-CONTAIN-1/2/3 are satisfied (Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching are declared children of InMotion in both source and closed model) so omitted. Cardinality binds owner=InMotion with member_domain=direct_child_states (three named substates), status=exact. The NL2-DISJOINT-1 guard_disjointness contract is a genuine structural concern: InMotion's two outgoing alternatives (to Stopping vs to EmergencyStopping) are realized in the closed model purely via a shared internal integer route-token (R45RouteToken==6 vs ==7) set by lower-level transitions rather than by the two named distinguishable events/conditions (arrival vs obstacle) directly on InMotion's own transitions -- the group structure is preserved but the actual mechanism collapses the semantic differentiation into an opaque encoding, which is a structural contrast worth flagging as predicate-null W1. I also note the InMotion group's declared owner-level transitions (line 35/36) are guarded by an internal control variable rather than carrying the named NL events directly, which is a group-level trigger/guard fidelity gap; I raise this as a derived transition-group-relation contract distinct from the individually-satisfied endpoint existence.

cardinality_bindings.reason: NL4 directly enumerates and counts three named direct child substates (Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching) owned by InMotion; this is a direct_child_states cardinality obligation, not a region-count obligation. The exact source inventory confirms InMotion (source_id InMotion) as parent of exactly these three child state rows (InMotion.Accelerating, InMotion.Cruising, InMotion.Approaching), and the closed ModelIR (state:InMotion:line:9) owns Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching/UnspecifiedInitial as direct children, giving the deterministic frontier the exact owner and domain needed to enumerate and compare against the required_count=3.

branches.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequence: root reachability of InMotion's substates, event-consumer coverage for Reached_Cruising_Cruise/Approached_Decelerate/Obstacle_Detected, forbidden/malformed initial entry into InMotion (UnspecifiedInitial instead of Accelerating), stable termination for Stopping/EmergencyStopping, and consistency between InMotion's outer route-token transitions and the substates' own [*] exits. The closed FCSTM shows InMotion has an internal initial edge to a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state rather than to Accelerating, and Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching are all unreachable from the root per inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts. This breaks NL5-INIT-1 (InMotion-local initial entry into Accelerating), and cascades into unreachable consumer coverage for the Reached_Cruising_Cruise and Approached_Decelerate events (NL5-ENDPOINT-1, NL6-ENDPOINT-1, NL7-ENDPOINT-1 endpoints exist syntactically but are dead code), the entry/do actions on Accelerating/Approaching (NL8-ACTION-1, NL9-STATEACTION-1, NL9-EFFECT-1, NL3 effect/action are reachable via UnspecifiedInitial->[*] route tokens so EmergencyStopping/Stopping remain reachable), and retention NL10. I also examine termination stability for Stopping and EmergencyStopping (both route to [*] with no re-entry, so termination is stable) and forbidden-scope entry (obstacle-detected event consumer coverage in InMotion scope is only reachable via UnspecifiedInitial, not via Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching, which is a distinct consumer-coverage gap already captured by NL2-DERIVED and NL3-DERIVED). I add one derived initial_entry contract targeting the malformed nested edge, since the existing NL5-INIT-1 already captures this exact obligation but I still bind evidence precisely against it rather than fabricating a new one where an existing exact contract suffices.
